title: Young players lack training; big bands return

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Do you ever hear any young trumpet players you think are good?

Oh, there are quite a few of them, quite a few of them, yes. Quite a few. But they haven't got the same interest in music. As soon as -- well, I'll tell you what happened at the Amsterdam one time. There was a woman there that -- of course, we have women that are members now, they're musicians. And women are in everything now.

And this woman was teaching a bunch of young kids, every Thursday afternoon, I think, at the club. So I was asked to come around there one time. And I had nothing to do that afternoon. I wanted to see them, like that.
Well, they're nice little kids. But as soon as they learned how to play the scale, they wouldn't come back anymore. Now, I got interested then, and I paid attention to some of the

older ones that were really playing. Those guys used to come in and play like hell. When you put something in front of them, they couldn't even read it. That bebop did all that. It's so much noise, and as long as you (singing), oh, they was jumping all around. Oh, he's great and all like that.

You sit them down at the stand there and put some music and tell them to play it, they look at you and say, I can't play it. If you took a tape of some of the things that he was playing all the time and put it in front of him, he couldn't play it. No, he couldn't play it.
See, they think they're musicians too soon. They jump too soon. They haven't got the proper training. They're not thorough enough.
For one thing, there aren't the big bands. I guess that was a very good training ground.

Yes, yes, yes. I like to see them coming back, because you watch those guys in those big bands. They know what the score is. They know what the score is. They can play. All you got to do -- of course, you don't go on the television or make a record unless you rehearse it yourself, because there might be a little this and that you have to correct.
